item.title: Environmental Narrative - Storytelling Through Environment
item.description:
Environmental Narrative - Storytelling Through Environment

← Back to Map Layouts | Index | Next: Loot Distribution →

🎭 Environmental Storytelling Philosophy

Principle: The world tells the story itself - no need for lengthy cutscenes.

Methods:

  • Visual clues (traces, items, graffiti)
  • Audio logs (short recordings 30-60s)
  • Environmental contrasts
  • Implied history through decay

🏭 Industrial Decay - Regional Stories

Reactor Tower - “The Meltdown”

Lore Background: Year 2029, the Power Plant was operating normally. When The Collapse occurred, the cooling system was hacked. Workers attempted a manual shutdown, but the radiation leak had already spread.

Environmental Traces:

Location Trace Implication
Floor 1 Worker corpses in protective suits Attempted manual shutdown
Floor 2 Barricade made of equipment Workers trapped above
Floor 3 Control panels destroyed Sabotage or panic
Basement Bloodtrail leading to tunnel Survivors escaped

Audio Log #1: “Final Shift”

“This is Foreman Lee… Day 3 after the lockdown. The radiation is rising. We sealed the lower levels but… [static] …Martinez didn’t make it. If anyone finds this, the emergency tunnel leads to the workshops. Don’t trust the—” [cut off]

Visual Details:

  • Clock stopped at 3:47 AM
  • Wall calendar: March 15, 2031
  • Emergency lights still flickering (separate generator)
  • Radiation warning signs freshly painted in red

Tech Labs - “Project Prometheus”

Lore Background: Secret research facility of Nexus Corporation. They were developing “Prometheus” - AI technology for human enhancement. The Outbreak might be related to escaped test subjects.

Environmental Traces:

Building Trace Implication
Lab Alpha Cages broken from the inside Test subjects escaped
Lab Beta Research notes burnt Cover-up attempt
Lab Gamma Bodies in hazmat suits Containment failed

Audio Log #2: “Dr. Chen’s Warning”

“Log 847. The Prometheus subjects are showing… unexpected behavior. Enhanced aggression, reduced pain response. I’ve recommended immediate termination but Director Park insists we continue. If this gets out… God help us all.”

Visual Details:

  • “SUBJECT 7” graffiti in dried blood
  • Broken glass from inside the cell
  • Medical equipment intentionally destroyed
  • Vaccine vials scattered (quest item hint)

Warehouse District - “The Smugglers’ Haven”

Lore Background: After The Collapse, the warehouse became a hub for smuggling. The Underground Network used to base here before moving.

Environmental Traces:

Warehouse Trace Implication
W1 Vehicle under repair Escape attempt
W2 Hidden weapon cache Smuggler stash
W3 Medical supply boxes Aid distribution
W4 Smashed electronics Rage or looting
W5 Sleeping bags, canned food Survivor camp
W6 Hazmat equipment Contamination warning

Audio Log #3: “Broker’s Message”

“To anyone listening on frequency 7: The Network is moving operations. Too much heat from Peacekeepers. If you need supplies, check W2 - leave something useful in exchange. Fair trades keep us alive. Remember: Trust no one, but trust us less.”

Office Complex - “Corporate Collapse”

Lore Background: Regional headquarters of Nexus Corp. When everything fell apart, executives tried to evacuate via the roof helipad - unsuccessfully.

Environmental Traces:

Floor Trace Implication
5F Helicopter crashed on roof Failed evacuation
4F Computers still on, data wiping Cover-up incomplete
3F Family photos, personal items Workers fled fast
2F Broken safes Looting aftermath
1F Barricades, bullet holes Someone made a stand

Audio Log #4: “Last Executive”

“This is CFO Thompson. The helicopter is not coming. Park… that bastard took the only evac for himself and his family. The rest of us are expendable. Security is breaking down… I can hear them in the stairwell. To my wife: I’m sorry. The vault code is—” [gunfire, static]

🩸 Bloodstain Storytelling Guide

Bloodstain Types & Meanings

Type Visual Story Implication
Splatter Radial pattern Violence, gunfire
Pool Large static puddle Body rested here
Drag Mark Linear streak Body moved
Handprint Palm on wall Wounded person walking
Footprints Bloody shoe marks Walker through blood

Placement Guidelines

DO:

  • Lead to loot locations (reward exploration)
  • Create implied narratives
  • Vary from old (brown) to recent (red)
  • Connect to audio logs

DON’T:

  • Excessive gore without purpose
  • Random placement
  • Near spawn areas (immersion break)
  • Child-related violence

🎨 Atmospheric Design Per Zone

Industrial Decay Atmosphere Palette

Zone Light Sound Mood
Reactor Red emergency, flickering Geiger counter, dripping Dread, urgency
Labs Clinical white, broken Machinery hum, alarms Unease, mystery
Warehouse Natural (holes in roof) Wind, metal creaking Isolation
Office Dim, monitors glow Static, distant gunfire Abandonment
Forest Dappled sunlight Birds, leaves Relief (deceptive)

📜 Graffiti & Environmental Text

Graffiti Categories

Survivor Messages:

  • “DAY 47 - NO HELP COMING”
  • “WATER IS SAFE - FOOD IS NOT”
  • “PEACEKEEPERS = MURDERERS”
  • “THE BROKER KNOWS”

Faction Tags:

  • ⚙️ Salvage Corps gear symbol
  • 👁️ Tech Syndicate eye pattern
  • 🤝 Underground Network hands
  • 🛡️ Peacekeepers shield

Warning Signs:

  • “RADIATION - DO NOT ENTER”
  • “SCAVS AHEAD”
  • “TRAP - GO AROUND”
  • “DEAD END”

🔊 Audio Log Distribution

Per Map Allocation

Map Total Logs Faction Focus Themes
Industrial Decay 15 Mixed Origin of Collapse
Urban Ruins 12 Survivors Daily survival
Military Base 10 Peacekeepers Final orders

Audio Log Template 

[LOG ID]: [Title]
Speaker: [Name, Role]
Duration: 30-60 seconds
Location: [Specific POI]
Trigger: Interact with [Object]

---
Script:
[30-60 second monologue with environmental sounds]
---

Lore Revealed:
- [Point 1]
- [Point 2]

Quest Connection: [If applicable]

🎯 Environmental Puzzle Hints

Hidden Loot Clues

Pattern: Environmental details hint at nearby secrets.

Examples:

Clue Location Secret
Arrow graffiti Warehouse W5 Hidden floor cache
Scratched wall numbers Office 3F Safe code nearby
Candles lit in circle Lab basement Special item spawn
Fresh bloodtrail Any Recent PvP happened here

item.title: Environmental Narrative Guidelines: "Show, Don't Tell"
item.description:
Environmental Narrative Guidelines: “Show, Don’t Tell”

← Back to Index | Visual Style

🏛️ The Silent Storyteller

Our world, Aethelgard, is dead. There are no safe zones for NPCs to give quests. The environment must be the primary method of delivering lore and plot.

Core Principle: “The Aftermath”

Every location should look like something happened there right before the player arrived. Avoid static, perfect presets.

🔍 Narrative Layers

Layer 1: The Panic (Immediate Past)

Shows the moment society collapsed.

  • Asset: Suitcases spilled open on a highway.
  • Implication: People fled in a hurry.
  • Asset: Half-eaten meals on a restaurant table.
  • Implication: The disaster struck instantly, unexpectedly.
  • Asset: Cars crashed into barricades, not just parked.
  • Implication: Drivers were desperate or terrified.

Layer 2: The Struggle (Recent Past)

Shows survivors trying to live in the ruins.

  • Asset: A mattress in a bank vault.
  • Implication: Someone thought money would keep them safe, or the thick walls were shelter.
  • Asset: Rain collectors made of tarps.
  • Implication: Water systems failed; desperation set in.
  • Asset: Makeshift graves in a playground.
  • Implication: High casualties; no space or time for proper burial.

Layer 3: The Decay (Present)

Shows nature reclaiming the world.

  • Asset: Trees growing through office floors.
  • Implication: It’s been years, not days.
  • Asset: Rust streaks dripping down concrete.
  • Implication: Maintenance stopped long ago.
  • Asset: Animals nesting in vehicle engines.
  • Implication: Wildlife no longer fears machinery.

🖼️ “Micro-Stories” (Vignettes)

Create small, self-contained scenes (dioramas) within the larger level.

Example A: The Last Stand

  • Setting: A bathroom stall in a subway station.
  • Props: A skeleton clutching a revolver. One spent casing on the floor. Door barricaded from the inside.
  • Story: A survivor hid here, heard the monsters coming, realized escape was impossible, and took their own way out. NO TEXT LOG NEEDED.

Example B: The Deal Gone Wrong

  • Setting: An alleyway behind a pharmacy.
  • Props: Two skeletons facing each other. A duffel bag of meds between them. Both have knives in their chests.
  • Story: A trade turned violent. Greed killed both parties. The loot (meds) is still there for the player.

Example C: The Hopeless Signal

  • Setting: A rooftop with a generator and radio tower.
  • Props: “SOS” painted in white on the roof. The generator is out of fuel. A skeleton sits by the radio, headphones on.
  • Story: Someone waited for rescue that never came.

📦 Loot Logic (Diegetic Placement)

Loot must make sense in its context. This rewards players who read the environment.

  • Medical Loot: DO NOT put medkits in random wooden crates. Put them in:
    • Ambulances
    • Bathrooms (cabinets)
    • Triage tents
    • Offices (First Aid wall boxes)
  • Weapon Parts: found on workbenches, gun store ruins, police trunks.
  • Food: Kitchens, supermarkets, vending machines (broken).

🔦 Lighting as Narrative

Use lighting to highlight these stories, but also to set the emotional tone.

  • Red Light: Danger, emergency, “Do Not Enter”. (Naturally attracts players due to curiosity).
  • Green Light: Safety, medical, “Exit”.
  • Flickering Light: Instability, recent damage, tension. (e.g., A light flickering near a vent suggests something is moving inside the vent).

🚫 Narrative Anti-Patterns

  1. Written Notes everywhere: Avoid “My Dearest Diary…” pages scattered in illogical places. Use environmental clues first.
  2. Blood without a Body: If there is a massive blood trail, it must lead somewhere (a body, a drag mark, a monster den). It cannot just end at a wall.
  3. Perfect Skeletons: Skeletons should be disarticulated, scavenged by animals, or crushed. Avoid the “Halloween Prop” look.

item.title: Map Design: Industrial Zone (The "Factory")
item.description:
Map Design: Industrial Zone (The “Factory”)

← Back to Index | Next: Art Direction →

🗺️ Map Overview

  • Name: Sector 7 Industrial Complex (aka “The Factory”)
  • Theme: Abandoned Soviet-era processing plant repurposed for anomalous research.
  • Size: Medium (1200m x 1200m)
  • Player Count: 12 Players (Solo/Duo/Squads) + 20 AI Bots
  • Raid Time: 20 Minutes
  • Difficulty: Intermediate (Balanced Loot/Risk)

Narrative Context: Once the primary refining facility for local crystalline resources. When the “Outbreak” occurred, the military sealed the exits, trapping workers inside. Now, it’s a scavenger’s paradise filled with raw materials, left-behind military gear, and dangerous chemical leaks.

📍 Tactical Layout

The map is a “Bowl” design: High ground on the perimeter (Forest/Hills), low ground in the center (Factory Complex), promoting inward movement.

       [Forest/Hills] (High Ground)
      /      |       \
     /   [Train Yard] \
    |         |        |
[Storage]--[BRIDGE]--[OFFICES]
    |         |        |
    |      [FACTORY]---|
    |      (Low/Hot)   |
[Parking]----|----[Main Gate]
    |        |         |
    \    [Perimeter]   /
     \_______|________/

Zone 1: The Perimeter (Green Zone)

Safe start, low loot, long sightlines.

  • 1A. Train Yard (North): Rusted cargo trains. Good linear cover. Sniper vantage points on train cars.
  • 1B. Storage Units (West): Rows of garage-style storage. Close-quarters combat (CQC). “Rat” looting spots.
  • 1C. Parking Lot (South): Abandoned civilian cars. Open area, hazardous to cross.

Zone 2: The Complex (Yellow Zone)

Moderate risk, industrial combat, verticality.

  • 2A. Assembly Hall: Huge open interior with conveyor belts. 2 levels (Ground + Catwalks). High verticality.
  • 2B. Offices: 3-story brick building attached to the hall. Tight corridors, breaching doors, filing cabinets (Intel loot).
  • 2C. Cooling Towers: Two massive towers. External spiral stairs leading to high ground sniping spots.

Zone 3: The Lab (Red Zone / Hotspot)

Extreme risk, highest tier loot, Boss spawn.

  • Location: Underground, accessible via 2A Assembly Hall elevator shaft or 2B Office basement.
  • Layout: Claustrophobic white corridors, broken glass, flickering lights.
  • Threats: High-level AI guards, The “Warden” (Boss).
  • Loot: Keycards, Injectors, High-tech weapon parts.

🛠️ Operator Tactical Interactions

Each class can exploit the map’s industrial nature differently:

Class Interaction Benefit Location Examples
TANK Heavy Breach Smash through weak brick walls or force open rusted gates. Offices (1F): Create new entry points. Storage: Break metal shutters.
RECON Signal Hack Hack CCTV cameras to reveal enemies on minimap for 30s. Security Room (offices), Factory Main Gate.
SPECIALIST Generator Overload Turn on/off industrial lights or electrified water hazards. Cooling Towers: Create noise cover. Canal: Electrify water to kill rushers.
SUPPORT Cargo Lift Can operate heavy elevators to move squad vertically. Assembly Hall: Move team to catwalks silently.
  • Destructible Environment: Catwalk railings can be shot out to drop enemies; Oil drums explode.

💎 Loot Distribution & Heatmap

Area / POI Loot Tier Item Types Danger Level Recommended For
The Lab (Underground) S-Tier (Highest) Keycards, Boss Gear, Injectors 💀 Extreme (Boss + Players) Squads / Geared Solos
Assembly Hall A-Tier (High) Weapon Parts, Industrial Tech 🔴 High (Sniper Sightlines) PvP Seekers
Offices B-Tier (Mid) Intel Items, Meds, Cash 🟠 Medium (CQC Ambush) Solos / Scavengers
Train Yard C-Tier (Low) Ammo, Basic Components 🟢 Low (Perimeter Spawn) Fresh Spawns / Snipe setup
Storage Units C-Tier (Low) Food, Construction Materials 🟢 Low (Good Cover) “Rat” Runs
  • Hotspot: The Lab entrance (Assembly Hall) attracts 70% of players eventually.
  • Safe Route: Skirting the perimeter from Storage → Train Yard → Gate 03 avoids most conflict but yields poor loot.

⚔️ Choke Points & Flow

Extraction shooters live and die by their Choke Points - areas where players are forced to interact.

1. “The Bridge” (Connecting West Storage to Factory)

  • Description: A narrow metal skybridge over a chemical canal.
  • Tactical: The only direct path from West Spawn to the Hotspot without going through the open canal (slow movement).
  • Danger: High. Easy to camp from the Office windows.

2. “Main Gate” (Factory Entrance)

  • Description: The primary reinforced gate into the compound. Slightly open, creating a funnel.
  • Tactical: High traffic area for vehicles (future) or squads rushing the center.
  • Danger: Variable. AI Scavs often patrol here.

3. “The Vent” (Lab Entrance)

  • Description: A destructible ventilation grate leading into the Lab.
  • Tactical: Requires explosives or a crowbar to open. Noisy entry.
  • Danger: Extreme. “Dinner bell” for nearby players.

🚪 Extraction Points

Name Type Requirements Location
Gate 03 Always Open None East Road (Perimeter)
Sewer Conditional No Backpack Central Canal (Under bridge)
Helipad Signal Flare Gun (Calls Heli, waits 2m) Rooftop of Assembly Hall
Armored Truck Paid 3000 Credits Front Gate (North)

🎨 Environmental Design & Atmosphere

Visual Identity

  • Palette: Rust Orange, Concrete Grey, Toxic Green (Chemicals).
  • Lighting: Overcast day (Standard). Interiors are dim, requiring flashlights/NVGs in the Lab.
  • Details:
    • Storytelling: “Help Us” painted on the roof.
    • Assets: Forklifts, pallets of rotting supplies, military checkpoints.

Audio Landscape

  • Ambient: Distant humming of the generator (directional clue), dripping water in tunnels, crows cawing outside.
  • Surfaces:
    • Metal (Catwalks): Loud, clanky. punishment for sprinting.
    • Glass (Offices): Crunching noise (Crucial for hearing flankers).
    • Puddles (Canal): Splashing sounds.

🗓️ Evolution Plan (Live Ops)

  • Phase 1 (Launch): Ground floor & 1st floor only. Lab sealed.
  • Phase 2: The “Lab” opens. New Boss added.
  • Phase 3: Dynamic Event - “Chemical Leak” floods the lower tunnels, forcing players to high ground.

item.title: Map Design: Neon Slums (The "Undercity")
item.description:
Map Design: Neon Slums (The “Undercity”)

← Back to Index | Next: Art Direction →

🗺️ Map Overview

  • Name: District 09 (aka “Neon Slums”)
  • Theme: Cyberpunk-favela built on the ruins of a mega-city. Dense, vertical, and neon-lit.
  • Size: Small/Dense (800m x 800m)
  • Player Count: 8 Players (Focus on Solo/Duo)
  • Raid Time: 15 Minutes
  • Difficulty: High (CQC focus, relentless verticality)

Unique Feature: Dynamic Day/Night Cycle. The raid starts at dusk and ends in pitch black night, forcing players to use flashlights or NVGs in the final minutes.

📍 Tactical Layout

The map is a “Favela” design: Layers built on top of layers. rooftops are highways; streets are death traps.

 LEVEL 3: [PENTHOUSE] (Sniper Nest)
              |
              | (Elevator/Scaffolding)
              |
 LEVEL 2: [Apt Block A]--[BRIDGE]--[Apt Block B]--[Arcade]
              |            |            |
              | (Stairs)   | (Jump)     | (Ramp)
              |            v            |
 LEVEL 1: [Market]----[Canal]----[Alleyways]
              |
              | (Stairs)
              v
 LEVEL 0: [Subway Station] (Underground)

Zone 1: The Gutters (Street Level)

Safe spawns, but dangerous to traverse.

  • 1A. The Market: Narrow alleyways cluttered with stalls. High occlusion (easy to hide, hard to see far).
  • 1B. Sewage Canal: Runs through the center. Slow movement speed deep water.
  • 1C. Subway Entrance: Only access to the localized underground metro station (Mid-tier loot).

Zone 2: The Stacks (Apartments)

Room-to-room combat, ambush heaven.

  • 2A. Apartment Block A & B: 4-story buildings connected by makeshift bridges. Destructible walls.
  • 2B. The Arcade: Neon-filled gaming hall. Loud ambient noise (distracts from footsteps). Good energy weapon loot.

Zone 3: The Penthouse (Hotspot)

Highest ground, sniper paradise.

  • Location: Top of the central skyscraper ruin. Accessible only via elevator (noisy) or external scaffolding (exposed).
  • Threats: Elite Sniper AI.
  • Loot: Data Chips, Legendary Sniper Parts.

🛠️ Operator Tactical Interactions

Navigating the vertical favela requires special tools:

Class Interaction Benefit Location Examples
RECON Zipline Setup Shoot a temporary zipline for the whole team. Rooftops: Cross between Apartment A and B instantly.
ASSAULT Parkour Leap Jump further/higher to reach hidden balconies. Alleyways: Reach 2nd floor windows without stairs.
SPECIALIST Drone Vent Send drones through small AC vents to scout rooms. Penthouse: Check for campers before breaching.
TANK Shield Wall Deploy portable cover on narrow bridges. Bridge of Sighs: Block sniper fire while crossing.
  • Cyber-Hacks: Hack neon signs to overload/explode them (Blind enemies). Hack Subway gates to lock sections.

💎 Loot Distribution & Heatmap (Verticality Focus)

Floor / Area Loot Tier Item Types Danger Level Recommended Key
Penthouse (Lvl 3) S-Tier Legendary Sniper Rifles 💀 Extreme (1 Entry point) King of the Hill
Arcade (Lvl 2) A-Tier Electronics, Energy Cells 🔴 High (Loud Audio) Balanced Squads
Apartments (Lvl 2) B-Tier Domestic Items, Cash 🟠 Medium (Wallbangs) Campers / CQC
Market (Lvl 1) C-Tier Food, Trash Loot 🔴 High (Visible from above) Risky Transit
Subway (Lvl 0) B-Tier Tools, Quest Items 🟠 Medium (Grenade traps) Flank Route
  • Heatmap: Most deaths occur at the “Bridge of Sighs” and the Subway Entrance.
  • The Trap: The Market (Street Level) has low-tier loot but high danger from rooftop snipers. Avoid lingering here.

⚔️ Choke Points & Flow

1. “Bridge of Sighs” (Connecting Apt A & B)

  • Description: A rickety wooden bridge connecting the 3rd floors of the two main buildings.
  • Tactical: Fastest way to cross without dropping to street level.
  • Danger: Exposed to snipers from The Penthouse.

2. “The Metro Turnstile”

  • Description: Narrow entrance to the subway.
  • Danger: Grenade trap heaven.

🚪 Extraction Points

Name Type Requirements Location
Subway Train Timed Arrives every 5 mins Underground Station
Rooftop Zipper Conditional Zipline Tool Required Apartment B Roof
Sewer Grate Always Open None Canal Finish Line

🎨 Environmental Design

  • Palette: Neon Pink/Blue, Dirty Concrete, Rain-slicked Asphalt.
  • Lighting: High contrast. Dark shadows vs blinding neon signs.
  • Audio: Constant rain (muffles light footsteps), distant sirens, cyberpunk synth music in the Arcade.

item.title: Map Design: The Mire (Wilderness Zone)
item.description:
Map Design: The Mire (Wilderness Zone)

← Back to Index | Next: Art Direction →

🗺️ Map Overview

  • Name: The Exclusion Mire (aka “The Swamp”)
  • Theme: Flooded forest reclaiming a failed biological test site. Foggy, treacherous terrain.
  • Size: Large (2000m x 2000m)
  • Player Count: 16 Players (Duo/Squad Focus)
  • Raid Time: 30 Minutes
  • Difficulty: Expert (Map knowledge critical for survival)

Unique Feature: Dynamic Water Level. Water rises and recedes slowly. Lootable areas become deadly traps; new paths open up.

📍 Tactical Layout

The map is a “Archipelago” design: Small islands of dry land connected by shallow water (slows movement) or deep channels (requires swimming/boat).

   [Hills]      [Old Road]
      |            |
 [Crash Site]--[Swamp Water]--[Sunken Village]
      |            |             |
      |       [Deep Lake]        |
      |            |             |
 [Fishing Huts]---[BIODOME]----[Watchtower]
      |            (Lab)         |
      \____________|_____________/
              [Forest Mud]

Zone 1: The Crash Site (West)

Spawn area, basic loot.

  • 1A. Plane Wreckage: A crashed military transport. Cover is sparse but metal offers protection.
  • 1B. Fishing Huts: Decaying wooden structures. Good for ambushes.
  • 1C. The Tree Line: Dense foliage limiting visibility to 20m.

Zone 2: The Marshlands (Center)

Dangerous crossing, high risk of getting stuck.

  • 2A. Sunken Village: Roofs are the only safe ground. Falling into water = huge noise + slow.
  • 2B. The Watchtower: Only high ground in the map. Perfect vision, zero cover.

Zone 3: Bio-Dome Alpha (Hotspot)

Sealed environment, chemical hazards.

  • Location: Center of the deepest lake. Accessible by bridge (exposed) or underwater pipe (requires Rebreather).
  • Layout: Clean, white lab interiors contrasting with the muddy exterior.
  • Threats: Mutated AI wildlife (fast, melee focus).
  • Loot: Bio-samples, High-value medical injectors.

🛠️ Operator Tactical Interactions

Surviving nature requires specific skills:

Class Interaction Benefit Location Examples
SUPPORT Bridge Layer Deploy a temporary plank bridge over mud/gaps. Swamp Channels: Cross silently without swimming.
TANK Heavy Removal Lift fallen logs blocking paths or loot. Forest Paths: Open shortcuts.
RECON Camouflage Net Set up a hidden observation post (invisible to thermal). The Watchtower: Ambush setup.
SPECIALIST Water Purify Turn toxic water into a stamina-boosting drink (Consumable). Bio-Dome: Heal effects of poison.
  • Trap Crafting: Recons can rig tripwires on narrow swamp paths.

💎 Loot Distribution & Heatmap

Area / POI Loot Tier Item Types Complexity / Risk Best Equipment
Bio-Dome Alpha S-Tier Injectors, Stimpacks, Crafting Blueprints 💀 Max (Gas/Radiation) Hazmat Suit / Gas Mask
Watchtower A-Tier Marksman Rifles, High-Zoom Scopes 🔴 High (Exposed) Camouflage / Smoke
Sunken Village B-Tier Food, Tools, Scrap Metal 🟠 Medium (Movement penalty) Light Armor
Fishing Huts C-Tier Basic Meds, Keys 🟢 Safe (Perimeter) Any
Swamp Channels Trash Driftwood (Crafting) 🔴 High (Slow movement + No cover) Avoid if possible
  • Heatmap: High player density around “The Causeway” bridge.
  • Tactical Warning: Looting in deep water (Swamp Channels) is suicidal as water movement slows you by 40% and makes splashing noises.

⚔️ Choke Points & Flow

1. “The Causeway” (Bridge to Bio-Dome)

  • Description: A long, straight concrete bridge. No cover except broken cars.
  • Tactical: Suicide run for squads without smoke grenades.
  • Danger: Any sniper in the Watchtower controls this.

2. “Alligator Alley” (Shallow Channel)

  • Description: A narrow path through thick reeds.
  • Tactical: The stealthy approach.
  • Danger: Getting stuck in mud slows movement by 50%. Easy pickings for grenades.

🚪 Extraction Points

Name Type Requirements Location
Hovercraft One-Time Arrives if Signal Flare used North Marsh
Old Road Always Open None West Edge
Bunker Elevator Conditional Bio-Keycard Inside Bio-Dome

🎨 Environmental Design

  • Palette: Mud Brown, Sickly Green, Fog Grey.
  • Auditory Illusion: Sounds carry differently in fog. Gunshots sound closer than they are.
  • Hazards: Mutated leeches in water (Drain Stamina), Gas pockets.

item.title: World & Map Design
item.description:
World & Map Design

← Previous: Operators | Index | Next: Art Direction →

Map Design Philosophy

Core Principles:

  1. Readability - Top-down perspective requires clear visual hierarchy.
  2. Tactical Depth - Multiple routes, cover options, and vertical elements.
  3. Risk vs Reward - Loot quality scales with danger level.
  4. Memorable Landmarks - Facilitates easy navigation and team callouts.

Extraction-Shooter Specifics

Primary and secondary design factors adapted for the extraction genre, directly influencing zone layouts.

Primary Factors

  1. Verticality

    • Definition: How height and layers affect play, visibility, and flanking.
    • Application:
      • Hot Zones: High verticality (3+ floors, catwalks) for complex CQB and vertical ambushes.
      • Mid Zones: Moderate verticality (2 floors, accessible rooftops) for vantage points.
      • Edge Zones: Mostly ground level with natural elevation changes.

  2. Size

    • Definition: Horizontal scale relative to match duration (travel time vs. looting time).
    • Application:
      • Hot Zones: Condensed footprint with high asset density to force encounters.
      • Edge Zones: Expansive areas to allow safe spawning and initial movement.

  3. Population

    • Definition: Player and AI entity density per square meter.
    • Application:
      • Hot Zones: Maximum density (High player convergence + Elite AI squads).
      • Mid Zones: Medium density (Roaming AI patrols, transiting players).
      • Edge Zones: Low density (Scattered AI, spawning/extracting players).

Secondary Factors

  • Spawn/Exit Points: Primarily located in Edge Zones to force inward movement. Conditional high-risk exits (e.g., rooftop helipads) may exist in Hot Zones.
  • Event Pockets / POIs: Dynamic areas (Supply Drops, Contamination) that can temporarily transform safe Mid Zones into combat-heavy Hot Zones.
  • Line of Sight (LOS): Hot Zones feature frequent blind spots and LOS breaks for tactical movement; Edge Zones offer longer sightlines but less hard cover.
  • Navigator Elements: Ziplines, jump pads, and ladders are placed strategically to bridge Mid Zone gaps or provide rapid access to Hot Zone verticality.

Map Structure

Zone Types

1. Hot Zones (Center Areas)

Characteristics:

  • 60% loot spawn rate
  • Rare and Epic items
  • Heavy AI presence (10-15 enemies)
  • Multiple entry points (5-7)
  • Vertical gameplay (multi-floor buildings)

Examples:

  • Power Plant central reactor
  • Military Command Center
  • Tech Research Facility

Design Goals:

  • Create focal points for conflict
  • Reward brave players
  • Dynamic combat spaces

2. Mid Zones (Transition Areas)

Characteristics:

  • 40% loot spawn rate
  • Uncommon and Rare items
  • Moderate AI (5-8 enemies)
  • 3-4 entry points
  • Mixed indoor/outdoor environments

Examples:

  • Office buildings
  • Warehouses
  • Residential blocks
  • Industrial workshops

Design Goals:

  • Provide safer looting options
  • Connect hot zones to map edges
  • Offer tactical choices for engagement

3. Edge Zones (Perimeter)

Characteristics:

  • 20% loot spawn rate
  • Common items, basic supplies
  • Minimal AI (0-3 enemies)
  • Open areas
  • Near extraction points

Examples:

  • Forest perimeters
  • Parking lots
  • Abandoned camps
  • Roadways

Design Goals:

  • Safe spawn areas
  • Quick escape routes
  • Extraction defense positions

Map Layouts

Map 1: “Industrial Decay”

Theme: Abandoned industrial complex Size: 1600m x 1600m Player Capacity: 12-16 players Match Duration: 15 minutes

Layout Overview:

                    NORTH
       [Extraction]   [Extraction]
            |             |
    [Forest]--[Warehouse District]--[Forest]
        |           |            |
[Spawn]---[Offices]--[POWER]--[Labs]---[Spawn]
        |           | PLANT|       |
    [Parking]--[Workshops] --[Storage]
            |             |
       [Extraction]   [Extraction]
                    SOUTH

Key Locations:

1. Power Plant (Hot Zone - Center)

  • 4 floors
  • Central reactor room (best loot)
  • Catwalks and tight corridors
  • AI Boss: “Reactor Guardian”
  • Highly contested area

2. Warehouse District (Mid Zone - West)

  • 6 large warehouses
  • Open floor plans
  • Good cover density
  • Vehicle section (future update: drivable)

3. Tech Labs (Mid Zone - East)

  • Research facility
  • Clean rooms (sterile environment)
  • Quest items spawn here
  • Vertical gameplay (3 floors)

4. Office Complex (Mid Zone - North)

  • Corporate offices
  • Cubicle maze
  • Excellent ambush spots
  • Medium tier loot

5. Workshops (Mid Zone - South)

  • Industrial repair shops
  • Heavy machinery provides cover
  • Crafting materials abundant

6. Forest Perimeter (Edge Zone)

  • Natural cover (trees and rocks)
  • Fewer sightlines
  • Player spawn points
  • 4 extraction zones

Map 2: “Urban Ruins”

Theme: Post-disaster city zone Size: 1800m x 1800m Player Capacity: 16 players Match Duration: 15 minutes

Layout Overview:

         [Subway]--[Mall]--[Subway]
              |      |        |
    [Park]--[Apts]--[PLAZA]--[Hotel]
         |      |      |         |
[Extraction]--[Street]--[Street]--[Extraction]

Key Locations:

1. Central Plaza (Hot Zone)

  • Open square
  • Central fountain provides cover
  • Underground access points
  • Supply drop landing zone

2. Shopping Mall (Hot Zone)

  • 2 floors
  • Stores contain high density loot
  • Food court ambush point
  • Skylights (dynamic lighting effects)

3. Apartment Buildings (Mid Zone)

  • 5-story buildings
  • Room-to-room CQB combat
  • Balcony sniping positions
  • Stairwell choke points

4. Subway System (Mid Zone)

  • Underground tunnels network
  • Connects different map areas
  • Dark, close-quarters environment
  • Unique lighting challenges

5. Hotel (Mid Zone)

  • Luxury location styling
  • Lobbies, guest rooms, rooftop bar
  • Quest item spawns
  • defensible position for extraction

6. City Park (Edge Zone)

  • Trees and dense foliage
  • Open sightlines across paths
  • Extraction zones location

Map 3: “Desert Outpost” (Post-Launch)

Theme: Military desert base Size: 2000m x 2000m (larger, more open) Weather: Sandstorms (dynamic)

Key Features:

  • Long sightlines (sniper-friendly)
  • Vehicle spawns
  • Underground bunker system
  • Dynamic sandstorm reduces visibility

Map Elements

Points of Interest (POI)

Design Guidelines:

  • Each map: 12-15 major POIs
  • Spacing: 150-250m apart
  • Size variation: Small (single building) to Large (complex)
  • Unique identifiers (visual landmarks)

Naming Convention:

  • Memorable, short names
  • Easy radio callouts
  • Example: “Red Warehouse,” “Big Tower,” “Reactor”

Cover System

Cover Types:

Full Cover (100% protection)

  • Concrete walls
  • Thick pillars
  • Armored vehicles
  • Metal containers

Half Cover (60% protection)

  • Wooden crates
  • Low walls
  • Cars
  • Machinery

Soft Cover (30% protection)

  • Bushes (visual obstruction)
  • Chain fences
  • Thin walls
  • Destructible objects

Design Rules:

  • Never leave large open areas without cover
  • Cover spacing: 5-10m intervals
  • Mix cover heights
  • Consider top-down sightlines

Loot Distribution

Container Types:

1. Common Crates (Gray)

  • Spawn: Edge và Mid zones
  • Contents: Basic supplies, ammo, common weapons
  • Quantity: 100-150 per map

2. Military Lockers (Green)

  • Spawn: Mid zones
  • Contents: Uncommon weapons, armor, meds
  • Quantity: 60-80 per map

3. Rare Safes (Blue)

  • Spawn: Hot zones, hidden locations
  • Contents: Rare weapons, valuable items
  • Quantity: 20-30 per map
  • Require: Lockpick or Specialist ability

4. Epic Vaults (Purple)

  • Spawn: Hot zone centers
  • Contents: Epic+ items, quest items
  • Quantity: 5-8 per map
  • Require: Keycard (found in mid zones)

5. Legendary Cache (Gold)

  • Spawn: 1-2 per map, random locations
  • Contents: Legendary items guaranteed
  • Require: Special key or team effort

Extraction Zones

Per Map: 4-6 extraction points

Placement Rules:

  • Near map edges
  • 300-400m from hot zones
  • Cover available nearby
  • Multiple approach routes

Extraction Types:

1. Helicopter Extract

  • Visual: Helicopter landing
  • Duration: 30 seconds
  • Max players: 4
  • Audio cue: Helicopter sounds from far

2. Vehicle Extract

  • Visual: Armored truck
  • Duration: 30 seconds
  • Max players: 6
  • Audio cue: Engine sounds

3. Underground Tunnel

  • Visual: Manhole entrance
  • Duration: 45 seconds (slower)
  • Max players: 2 (bottleneck)
  • Audio cue: Metal clanging

Activation:

  • Random 2-3 active per match
  • Announced at 3-minute mark
  • Cannot be camped from spawn (protection timer)

Dynamic Elements

Supply Drops

  • Timing: 5:00 and 10:00 into match
  • Landing: Random mid-to-hot zones
  • Visual: Signal flare, followed by parachute drop
  • Audio: Plane flyover, warning siren
  • Contents: High-tier loot, special weapons/items
  • Radius: Creates temporary high-heat zone

Contamination Zone

  • Timing: Starts at 12:00
  • Effect: Shrinking safe zone
  • Visual: Red fog, particle effects
  • Damage: Increasing over time (10→50 HP/sec)
  • Purpose: Forces player movement, prevents camping

Environmental Hazards

1. Electrical Hazards

  • Exposed/Broken power lines
  • Sparking machinery
  • Damage: 5 HP/sec within area

2. Radiation Zones (Map-specific)

  • Contaminated areas
  • Damage: 10 HP/sec
  • Reward: Best loot located inside

3. Fire (Dynamic)

  • Can be caused by explosions
  • Spreads slowly
  • Damage: 15 HP/sec
  • Blocks paths

Environmental Storytelling

Narrative Through Environment:

Industrial Decay Map:

  • Abandoned worker belongings and personal items
  • Evacuation warning signs
  • Broken and rusted machinery
  • Graffiti from survivors or scavengers
  • Evidence of environmental disasters

Visual Clues:

  • Scattered documents (lore items)
  • Propaganda posters
  • Faction symbols and territorial markings
  • Timeline of events shown through decay levels

Purpose:

  • Build world lore
  • Create atmosphere
  • Deepen player immersion
  • Provide context for Quests

Verticality

Top-Down Considerations:

Multi-Floor Buildings:

  • Clear visual distinction per floor
  • Stairs và elevators (future)
  • Different loot per floor
  • Rooftop access

Visual Solutions:

  • Floor transparency when player above/below
  • Minimap floor indicators
  • Height markers on UI
  • Shadow effects

Gameplay Impact:

  • Sniper positions (rooftops)
  • Ambush from above
  • Escape routes (parkour future)

Navigation Design

Wayfinding:

Visual Landmarks:

  • Tall structures (towers, smokestacks)
  • Unique color schemes per area
  • Distinct lighting differences
  • Varied architectural styles

Minimap Design:

  • Color-coded zones
  • POI icons
  • Extraction markers
  • Player/enemy indicators
  • Scale appropriate for mobile screens

In-World Signs:

  • Directional signs (diegetic/in-universe)
  • Zone markers
  • Extraction indicators (visible from distance)

Spawn System

Spawn Points:

  • 8-12 spawn locations per map
  • Located near map edges only
  • Equidistant from hot zones (fairness)
  • Random assignment
  • 10-second protection shield

Spawn Balancing:

  • No spawns near active combat
  • Distance check from other players (minimum 100m)
  • Visibility check (not in direct sightline)

Map Balance Metrics

Target Metrics:

Loot Distribution:

  • Common items: 60%
  • Uncommon items: 25%
  • Rare items: 10%
  • Epic items: 4%
  • Legendary items: 1%

Combat Density:

  • Hot zones: 40% of kills
  • Mid zones: 45% of kills
  • Edge zones: 15% of kills

Extraction Success:

  • Per zone: 20-30% usage rate
  • No single zone dominates (>40%)

Heatmaps Tracking:

  • Player death locations
  • Loot pickup locations
  • Time spent per zone
  • Path travel frequency

Weather & Time of Day

Launch: Static day lighting

Post-Launch Features:

Weather System:

  • Clear (default)
  • Rain (reduced visibility, louder footsteps)
  • Fog (close-range combat favored)
  • Sandstorm (Desert map)

Time of Day:

  • Day (launch default)
  • Dusk (future - different aesthetics)
  • Night (future - flashlight mechanics)

Map Rotation & Voting

Launch:

  • 2 maps in rotation
  • Random selection

Post-Launch:

  • Map voting (3 options)
  • Weighted random (prevent repeats)
  • Featured map (events)

Level Design Checklist

For each new map:

Layout:

  • Balanced hot/mid/edge zones
  • Multiple routes between POIs
  • No dead-end areas
  • Extraction zone placement
  • Spawn point placement

Loot:

  • Container placement (200-300)
  • Rarity distribution balanced
  • Quest item locations
  • Supply drop landing zones

Combat:

  • Cover density appropriate
  • Sightline variety
  • Flanking routes available
  • Vertical elements considered

Navigation:

  • Visual landmarks present
  • Minimap readable
  • Wayfinding clear
  • Zone transitions smooth

Performance:

  • Occlusion volumes set
  • LOD configured
  • Draw calls optimized
  • Collision simplified

Playtesting:

  • 10+ internal playtests
  • Heatmap analysis
  • Balance adjustments
  • Bug fixes

Future Map Concepts

Map 4: “Flooded City”

  • Water mechanics
  • Boat navigation
  • Underwater areas

Map 5: “Mountain Facility”

  • Snowy environment
  • Cable cars
  • Avalanche hazards

Map 6: “Abandoned Airport”

  • Huge open tarmac
  • Airport terminals
  • Plane wrecks
